chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from his men, from Yunus, from them (peace be upon him), said:

Regarding the embalming of the deceased and his enshrouding, he said: Spread the wrapping cloth, then spread the loincloth upon it, then spread the shirt upon it and fold the front of the shirt over it. Then take camphor powder and place it on his forehead, the place of his prostration, and wipe the camphor over all his joints, from his head to his feet, and in his head, neck, shoulders, elbows, and in every joint of his hands and legs, and in the middle of his palms.

Then he is carried and placed upon his shirt, and the front of the shirt is folded over him, and the shirt should be without hemming or buttons. Two pieces of fresh palm stalks, each the length of an arm's span, are made for him: one is placed between his knees, half towards the shin and half towards the thigh, and the other is placed under his right armpit. Cotton or camphor is not placed in his nostrils, eyes, ears, or upon his face.

Then he is turbaned: the middle of the turban is taken and wrapped around his head in circles. The excess of the right side is cast over the left, and the left over the right, then it is extended over his chest.
ai.seo_question: What is the step-by-step Shia ritual for embalming and shrouding the deceased?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the precise ritual procedure for embalming (tahneet) and shrouding (takfin), emphasizing the application of camphor to the five major prayer joints to honor the body's readiness for prostration. It specifies the use of simple, unsewn garments and palm stalks, reflecting the Shia tradition of modesty and the belief that the deceased retains the spiritual significance of their earthly worship.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from his men, from Yunus, 
(It has been narrated) from them<sup>asws</sup>

having said regarding the embalming of the deceased and his enshrouding, said: ‘Spread the wrapping with a spreading. Then spread the loincloth upon it. Then spread the shirt upon it and fold the front of the shirt upon it. Then deliberate to the camphor powder and place it upon his forehead, the place of his prostrations, and wipe it with the camphor upon the entirety of his joints, from his head up to his feet, and in his head, and in his neck, and his shoulders, and his elbows, and in every joint from his joints, from the two hands and the two legs, and in the middle of his palms.

Then carry him and place him upon his shirt and fold the front of the shirt upon him, and the shirt should happen to be without any hemming or buttons, and make two pieces of wet branches to be for him, of an arm’s length, making one of it to be in between his knees, halfway from what follows the leg, and halfway from what follows the thigh, and make the other one to be under his right armpit, and do not make cotton or camphor to be in his nostrils, nor in his eyes, nor his ears, nor upon his face.

Then make a turban by taking the middle of the turban and wrapping it around his head in circles. Then cast the extra ends, the right one upon the left and the left one upon the right. Then extend it upon his chest’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from his people from Yunus from ’A’immah, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, who has said the following:

“About Hunut and shrouding a deceased, he (the Imam) has said, ‘Spread al-Hibrah (the large sheet of fabric), then spread the loincloth over which you then spread the shirt. Then turn back upward the front side of the shirt. Then find the ground camphor, place a certain amount of it over his forehead on the place for sajdah and then rub camphor over all of his joints from his head down to his toes, on his head, neck, shoulders, and elbows and on all of joints of his hands and legs and on the middle of his palms.

Then pick him up and place him on the shirt, then turn the front of the shirt over his front side. The shirt must not have any collar or buttons. Two fresh al-Jaridah (twigs of palm tree), one yard in length are placed with him. One is placed between his knees parallel with his leg and one-half of it parallel with his thigh and the other one under his right armpit. No cotton or camphor is placed in his nostril, eyes, and ears or on his forehead.

Then a turban is made for him. The center of the turban is placed on his head and then turned around his head, then the remaining is thrown on his shoulders in opposite sides by throwing the right to the left and the left to the right. Then the remaining is pulled over his chest.”’
